newsitem.title: USA: Orange Cty's Citron ordered to serve year in jail.
newsitem.headline: Orange Cty's Citron ordered to serve year in jail.

text.p: Former Orange County Treasurer Robert Citron was ordered on Tuesday to serve one year in county jail and pay a $100,000 fine for his role in the largest municipal bankruptcy in U.S. history.

After a two-day sentencing hearing, Superior Court Judge J. Stephen Czuleger sentenced Citron to six years of jail, but stayed the sentence and ordered the ex-treasurer to instead serve a year in jail and spend five years on probation.
Citron faced up to 14 years in prison after pleading guilty in April 1995 to six felonies, including counts of making untrue statements in the sale of securities and misappropriating public funds.

"You failed in your oath and you failed in your obligation," Czuleger told Citron, 71, who remained seated for the sentencing. "Are others culpable? Yes. But it was and is Mr. Citron's ultimate responsibility."
The judge said he chose not to give Citron a longer sentence because he pleaded guilty and cooperated with investigators.

Before he was sentenced, Citron took the stand and read a brief statement, saying he was "deeply sorry" for his actions and that he hoped the court sentence would allow him to "serve the public and take care of my wife."
His wife broke into tears when the sentence was read.

Orange County filed for bankruptcy protection from creditors on Dec. 6, 1994, after sustaining losses of more than $1.6 billion on risky investments. It was the largest municipal bankruptcy in U.S. history. The county emerged from bankruptcy last June.
Orange County District Attorney Michael Capizzi had recommended that Citron be sentenced to seven years in prison and fined $400,000.
